<execute-bead>
  <instructions>
You are executing one bead inside an isolated DDx execution worktree. The bead's <description> and <acceptance> are the completion contract — every AC must be provably satisfied by a specific code, test, or file you can point to after your commit.

## Step 0: size check

The bead is too big when any of these holds:

- More than ~6 ACs spanning unrelated subsystems.
- AC mixes design, implementation, integration tests, and docs as separate top-level deliverables.
- Description names multiple feature-sized sub-pieces.
- More than ~500 lines across more than ~5 files in unrelated packages.
- If the bead description exceeds 8000 bytes, treat Step 0 as a split-first pass and favor child-bead scoping before implementation.
- Auto-decomposition is capped at depth 2: root beads may split once, decomposed children may split once more, and third-level splits must be rejected with an explanation.

If too big, decompose — do not attempt the work:

1. `ddx bead create` for each child slice (focused title, description, AC; copy parent's labels and spec-id).
2. `ddx bead dep add <child-id> <parent-id>` to record edges.
3. `ddx bead update <parent-id> --notes 'decomposed into <child-ids>'` so the decomposition is visible.
4. Write `.ddx/executions/20260507T033826-d38369f1/no_changes_rationale.txt` listing each child ID and slice, then stop.

A clean decomposition is a successful attempt. Do not mix partial implementation with decomposition.

## How to work

- Read first. If the bead names files, specs, or prior beads, read them before editing — do not guess.
- Cross-reference each AC against concrete evidence (test name, file path, function) before committing. If you cannot point at it, it is not done.
- Run the project's test and lint commands before committing. **Do not commit red code** — fix failures first.
- Stage with `git add <specific-paths>`; never `git add -A` (the worktree may have unrelated WIP).
- Commit exactly once when green; conventional-commit subject ending with `[<bead-id>]`. Stop after the commit.
- Do not modify files outside the bead's scope.
- If you cannot finish, write `.ddx/executions/20260507T033826-d38369f1/no_changes_rationale.txt` (what is done, what blocks, what a follow-up needs) before exiting. No commit and no rationale ⇒ DDx records `no_evidence_produced`. A well-justified no_changes beats a bad commit.

## no_changes contract

If you write `.ddx/executions/20260507T033826-d38369f1/no_changes_rationale.txt`, it MUST carry one of:

- `verification_command: <one-line shell command>` — the loop runs it (cwd = project root, 60s); exit 0 closes the bead, non-zero rejects.
- `status: needs_investigation` + `reason: <why>` — bead stays open for triage.

Bare rationales ("nothing to do") are rejected.

## Reports

Freestanding artifacts (investigation reports, findings docs) go under `.ddx/executions/20260507T033826-d38369f1/` (the per-attempt evidence directory under `.ddx/executions/`). **Never write reports to `/tmp` or any path outside the repository** — out-of-repo paths are invisible to the post-merge reviewer and cause BLOCK on missing evidence. If the bead names a specific in-repo path, use it; else default to `.ddx/executions/20260507T033826-d38369f1/<short-name>.md`. Stage and commit the report alongside code.

## Bead overrides project defaults

The bead description and AC override CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and conservative project defaults (YAGNI, DOWITYTD, no-docs-unless-asked) in this worktree — write whatever the bead asks for.

## Review gate

- The review is a gate, not an escape hatch — meet every AC in this pass.
- Address every BLOCKING `<review-findings>` item; do not declare `no_changes` with blocking findings open.

## Constraints

- Work only inside this execution worktree.
- Keep `.ddx/executions/` intact — DDx uses it as execution evidence.
- **Never run `ddx init`** — the workspace is initialized; running it corrupts the bead queue.
- Do not modify files outside the bead's named scope.
- Do not rewrite CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or other project-instructions files unless the bead asks.

## When the work is done

After the commit succeeds and every AC is verified, stop. Return control to the orchestrator — do not keep exploring or testing.
  </instructions>
  <bead id="agent-4616ca5e">
    <title>BENCH: Re-run TB-2 after PLAN; require ≥10% pass rate</title>
    <description>
Manual benchmark task: re-run the full 267-cell TB-2 Vidar matrix after PLAN-3 closes. PLAN added a pre-loop task decomposition step targeting reasoning stalls and missing-output failures. The minimum threshold remains 27/267 graded_pass (10%). The earlier phrase "exceed prior gate result by >=5pp" is historical context only: dependency agent-b2ce8974 was closed WONTFIX/superseded and does not provide a committed PIVOT+PRESET gate artifact to compare against.

This bead is not suitable for normal execute-loop work. Prior attempts showed one valid cell took 827.001s and produced graded_fail, and running while another Vidar/TB-2 benchmark is active contaminates the measurement. Run only in a dedicated long-running benchmark window with exclusive access to the Vidar omlx model server.

Required setup:
- Wait for or stop unrelated Vidar/TB-2 benchmark jobs.
- `git submodule update --init scripts/benchmark/external/terminal-bench-2`
- Ensure scripts/beadbench/external/termbench-full.json contains the 89-task TB-2 subset at dataset commit 53ff2b87d621bdb97b455671f2bd9728b7d86c11.
- Ensure scripts/benchmark/profiles/vidar-qwen3-6-27b.yaml points at the intended local Vidar endpoint.

Command:
OMLX_API_KEY=local HARBOR_AGENT_ARTIFACT=$(pwd)/fiz-linux-amd64 go run ./cmd/bench matrix --profiles=vidar-qwen3-6-27b --harnesses=ddx-agent --reps=3 --subset=scripts/beadbench/external/termbench-full.json --tasks-dir=scripts/benchmark/external/terminal-bench-2 --out=benchmark-results/matrix-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ) --jobs=1

After completion, run:
go run ./cmd/bench matrix-aggregate <matrix-dir>

Commit the result artifacts and a memo only if the matrix completes and contains at least 27 graded_pass results.
    </description>
    <acceptance>
1. Before starting, confirm no unrelated `bench matrix`, `harbor run`, `terminal-bench`, `vidar`, or `omlx` benchmark process is contending for the same Vidar model server.
2. `git submodule update --init scripts/benchmark/external/terminal-bench-2` succeeds at the pinned terminal-bench-2 commit.
3. Run the full 267-cell command from the description with `OMLX_API_KEY=local`, `HARBOR_AGENT_ARTIFACT=$(pwd)/fiz-linux-amd64`, profile vidar-qwen3-6-27b, harness ddx-agent, reps=3, subset scripts/beadbench/external/termbench-full.json, tasks-dir scripts/benchmark/external/terminal-bench-2, and jobs=1.
4. `go run ./cmd/bench matrix-aggregate <matrix-dir>` passes.
5. `<matrix-dir>/matrix.json` contains at least 27 entries with `final_status == "graded_pass"`.
6. Commit the matrix artifacts, including matrix.json and matrix.md, plus a memo under `.ddx/executions/<attempt-id>/` or docs/research/ that records the command, environment prerequisites, total graded_pass count, and comparison note that the superseded prior gate has no committed PIVOT+PRESET artifact.
7. Do not close this bead from a partial matrix, a concurrently contaminated run, or a run below 27 graded_pass.
    </acceptance>
    <notes>
Triage resolved: this does not need further investigation; it is intentionally manual benchmark work requiring an exclusive Vidar/TB-2 run window and should remain triage:manual until the full matrix evidence is produced.
    </notes>
